title: Automated Legacy Codebase Migration
business: Enterprise software firms maintaining massive, aging code repositories.
problem: High operational costs and latency when using top-tier models for routine but complex refactoring tasks that do not require the absolute maximum reasoning capacity.
solution: GPT-6.1 Sol provides near-Astra performance for complex coding tasks, allowing teams to maintain high-quality refactoring outputs while optimizing resource allocation through its specific reasoning effort controls.
steps: Identify refactoring modules that require complex logic but fall within the 1,050,000 context window.
Configure the Responses API to utilize gpt-6.1-sol with reasoning.effort set to medium to balance depth and efficiency.
Implement the code_interpreter tool within the Responses API to validate refactored snippets against existing test suites.
Monitor performance outputs to determine if higher reasoning.effort settings are required for specific edge-case modules.
outcome: Teams achieve a sustainable balance between high-fidelity code refactoring and operational expenditure, maintaining architectural integrity without over-provisioning compute.
limitation: The model does not support minimal or none reasoning efforts, which may lead to unnecessary compute usage for trivial tasks; verify this by monitoring token consumption versus task complexity.

code.content:
client.responses.create(
  model="gpt-6.1-sol",
  messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Refactor this module"}],
  reasoning_effort="medium", # Set effort to balance performance and cost
  tools=[{"type": "code_interpreter"}] # Enable tool for validation
)
code.explanation: This snippet demonstrates configuring the model with a specific reasoning effort and enabling the code interpreter tool to ensure the refactored code is functional.
